subject: Request: strategic partner credits + discount combo (Acme Health) — exec approval needed
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Acme Health — combined credits + discount (exec approval)

Team,

Quick ask: Acme Health (large payer in Midwest) is asking for a combined exception: an introductory consumption credit package plus a higher-than-standard first-year discount to switch from a competitor before the end of Q4. Summary below — I need exec approval to commit from Commercial for their procurement/RFP timeline.

Why this matters
- Strategic reference: will be used in two upcoming RFP responses in healthcare, high visibility.
- Expected committed ARR: ~$350k ARR if they sign for 12 months after trial.
- Sales cadence: procurement wants numbers today to include in their internal scoring; legal needs SOW to start redlines.

Requested exception (by customer):
- Platform credits: $10,000 of consumption credits applied during the trial (first 90 days)
- Discount: 25% off list for first 12 months on the selected model route
- Commitment: 12-month minimum once trial converts; prefer a hard start date 30 days after SOW execution

Proposed counter (my recommendation):
- Approve $8,000 consumption credits (applied as account credits over 90 days)
- Approve 22% discount first year (instead of 25%)
- Require 12-month minimum and cancellation clause that credits are clawed back if they don’t convert

Attachments: RDW-deal-summary-ACME.xlsx, SOW-acme-draft.pdf (draft)
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

Asks:
1) Exec approval on the above counter (credits + discount)
2) Any legal/finance constraints I should know about before I send the counter to procurement

If we don’t sign this by end of week they will re-score the RFP and will likely slip to a competitor. Please reply with Approve/Decline/Counter and preferred cap on credits.

Thanks,
Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Vivek —
Quick clarifying Qs:
1) Are the requested credits strictly promotional consumption credits or do they expect cash rebates? We prefer credits.
2) Do they have a committed volume number? The $350k ARR you note — is that firm or an upper estimate?

My initial thought: $10k feels high for a first-time customer with no signed case studies. Can we push to $6–8k and 20–22% discount? If procurement is pushing hard and this is a strategic reference, we could stretch.

Please send the procurement contact and any procurement deadlines.

—Marissa

Marissa —
Answers below and added procurement contact.
1) Credits: they explicitly asked for platform consumption credits (not cash). They want credits to be visible in the invoice/quote so their finance can include it in TCO calculations.
2) ARR: $350k is our forecasted ARR based on the scope they shared (3 product routes, estimated 120k tokens/mo at present pricing). They verbally committed to the 12-month minimum during commercial discussions but haven't signed the SOW yet.

Procurement: Sarah Lawson, sarah.lawson@acmehealth.com (copied in later threads). Procurement timeline: they need numbers for their internal scoring matrix by EOD today.

Proposed final: $8,000 credits + 22% discount + 12-month min. If approved I will: 1) update SOW, 2) ask Legal to prioritize, 3) send to procurement with clear credit application language.

Vivek

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Request: Acme Health — combined credits + discount (exec approval)

Team —
I reviewed the pipeline math and the proposed concession. Recommendation: approve a bounded exception to accelerate close but include protective terms. Specifics I support:
- 22% first-year discount (cap to product routes in the quote)
- $8,000 in consumption credits applied during first 90 days
- 12-month minimum with a pro-rated clawback if they terminate before month 6 (clawback amount = remaining credit value pro-rated)
- Require a short addendum in the SOW that disallows transfer of credits and documents conversion triggers

If we sign we should also require a 60-day check-in to evaluate usage and potential upsell. This keeps the account team accountable.

If legal/finance signs off I think this is a net-positive. Approve pending legal language.

-Karthik
VP, Sales Operations

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>

Subject: Approval: Acme Health concession (conditional)

All —
I approve the commercial exception on the following conditions:
- Credits capped at $8,000 and applied as consumption credits over 90 days
- Discount capped at 22% for the first 12 months
- Clawback clause as Karthik outlined; finance to confirm clawback calculation and recognition treatment
- Legal to review SOW addendum and sign off on credit language

Evelyn — can you confirm we are okay from a finance/recognition perspective? If yes, I will greenlight Vivek to send the counter to Acme today.

Tessa Morgan
VP Sales
